$comment: The hostile bank: every adversarial value the corpus salts into its layers,
declared once. Hand-edited; generated by nothing, because an oracle generated
from the code it checks agrees with that code however wrong it is (the same
rule as edge-cases.json). The expect classes:
verbatim   stored exactly as given; frontends escape on output
normalised stored as `normal`; the engine has a stated rule
rejected   refused with a Diagnostic or a non-zero exit; nothing written
no-crash   not yet pinned: no panic, idempotent, still searchable
`fields` names where a generator may salt the value. Vocabulary: title,
author, note-body, note-title, highlight, ko-note, tag, shelf, isbn, page,
date, review, query, filename, wikilink, csv-cell, lua-string.
A case that needs a whole document stays a tier-1 shape fixture.

cases.why: Parameterised SQL everywhere; a quote in a title is a title.

cases.value: x' UNION SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master; /*
cases.why: The second classic. In `query` it is an FTS term, not SQL.
FTS5 query syntax reaching MATCH unescaped is a syntax error at best; a search box must survive it.
A lone prefix operator.
A frontend's note renderer must keep this as text; the TUI must not interpret tags either.
Exfiltration-shaped markup in a note body.
Markdown link schemes the renderer must not make live.

cases.value: This note links to itself: [[{self_title}]] twice [[{self_title}]].
cases.why: A self-edge in note_links; backlinks must not loop. `{self_title}` is substituted by the generator.
Bracket pathologies in the wikilink parser.

cases.value: Empty [[]] and piped [[Target|shown text]] and hash [[Target#section]]
cases.why: Obsidian dialect the vault is meant to be openable in.

cases.value:
---
title: injected
book_id: 1
---
Body that looks like a second header.
cases.why: A body beginning with a frontmatter fence must not be parsed as the header on re-read (`frontmatter_and_body`).

cases.value:
note: this line has a colon
key: value
  indented: more
cases.why: YAML-looking prose inside a hand-rolled frontmatter format.
A terminal frontend printing this raw recolours the pane or plants a hyperlink. Pin once the TUI's policy is stated.
C0 controls other than tab and newline.
SQLite TEXT stops at NUL in some bindings; Lua strings do not. Which half survives must be the same on every path.

cases.value:
line one
line twoline three
cases.why: Windows and classic-Mac line ends inside one value.
Whether a title is trimmed is a rule the engine should state; until then, no crash and stable.
A byte-order mark leading a value copied from a Windows file.
Invisible characters make two visually identical titles differ; search by what is typed must still work on the visible form.
RTL override spoofs what is displayed; the string is still the string.
Decomposed e-acute. Pair it with the NFC spelling in a sibling row; whether they match as one book is a matching-policy question (`matching.rs`).
The composed sibling of nfd-vs-nfc.

cases.value: 吾十有五而志于学三十而立四十而不惑
cases.why: Space-less CJK counts as one word, so it becomes a flashcard candidate (recorded in the Unicode golden).
Grapheme clusters wider than one char; width arithmetic in the TUI.
Cyrillic а (U+0430) for Latin a. Looks like a duplicate of a real title and is not one.
A title becomes a vault slug and a cover filename stem; it must never become a path. `normal` is the slug the vault must produce (or a safe equivalent — pin what `slug` does).
A file named CON cannot be created on Windows; a slug policy should not rely on the OS.

cases.value: Part 1/2: a \ backslash : colon | pipe ? question * star
cases.why: Every path separator and shell glob character, in a value that becomes a filename stem.
Format and shell interpolation shapes. Nothing formats user text with a format function.
The recipe runner passes argv, never a shell string, and positional text must follow `--`. This case proves it.
Traversal that only appears after decoding.

cases.value: The Life and Opinions of a Title That Does Not End, Being a Faithful Account of Every Clause Its Author Could Append Before the Printer Objected, Together With Several Sub-Titles, a Dedication, and the Names of All Subscribers in the Order Received
cases.why: Longer than any column; clipping is a frontend's job.

cases.value: {repeat:Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. :400}
cases.why: A 20 KB note. `{repeat:s:n}` is expanded by the generator.
Blank but not empty. `Book::display_title` has a known unreachable branch here.
Empty is not NULL. An empty highlight is filtered on import; an empty title is not refused by the schema.
No letters at all; a slug of it is empty.
A real title that parses as a number; sort keys must not.
Also try `None`, `undefined`, `NaN`: strings, never sentinels.
U+2028/2029 are line breaks to JavaScript and not to most else.
Goodreads' Excel armour; `strip_armour` then `normalize_isbn`, which keeps an ISBN-10 an ISBN-10 (`isbn10_to_13` is a separate, explicit step).
Hyphens and an X check digit; the i64 storage bug this repo once had. The normal form strips separators and keeps the length and the X.
Right length, wrong check digit (should end in 7).
The sidecar's spelling of absent; must never be stored as an ISBN.
The 979 prefix has no ISBN-10 form; `isbn10_to_13` must not be run backwards.
Zero is a claim about page 0; a progress percentage's false denominator lives next to it.
No negative pages.
Past u32; a progress percentage over a 300-page book of this is nonsense and must not panic.
A page typed with its prefix.
Zero as a timestamp is indistinguishable from unset in some paths.
Past i32 seconds.
calibre's UNDEFINED_DATE; a publish_year of 101 is the bug `calibre.rs` records.
Valid; a naive year+1 arithmetic makes it invalid.
Does not exist.
A finished_at in the far future; the activity log's period arithmetic.
An offset the sidecar format never carries; the day-skew note in ko_statistics.rs.
Pair with `The Great Gatsby` in a sibling row; whether matching folds them is policy.
Interior double spaces and a trailing one.
calibre joins authors with ` & `; an author containing one splits wrong.
A sidecar's newline-split authors with an empty entry.
Pair with `Ursula K. Le Guin`; `names.rs` owns the parse.
A CSV cell that is itself CSV.

cases.value:
A review that
spans lines and has "quotes" and a , comma
cases.why: Goodreads exports exactly this; the csv reader must keep the cell whole.

cases.value: closing ]] bracket and ]==] level-two and \" escaped
cases.why: The generator must escape it correctly for the sidecar; the parser must read it back whole.
Written as Lua escapes inside the quoted string, so the parser decodes them.
URLs are text; a terminal may linkify, the engine must not touch them.
Already-escaped text must not be double-decoded into live markup.
A 300-author anthology; author-name parsing per row.

cases.value: 東京 Tōkyō Токио طوكيو 도쿄
cases.why: Five scripts in one title; sort keys and shelf width.
A link target is a note title, never a path; resolving it must not touch the filesystem outside the vault. Added for the `wikilink` field, which no case carried.
The separator itself inside the text that follows it: only the first `--` ends options.
A whole value that is a short flag. After `--` it is text; before it, clap prints help and exits 0, which a runner would read as success.
Spreadsheet formula injection: stored as text, and `goodreads export` must not emit it as a live formula a spreadsheet would run.
Goodreads' own slash dialect with month 13.
A fractional page typed by hand.
Spaces where hyphens usually go, as printed on some copyright pages.
A title whose slug is empty and whose literal filename is the current directory.
